About Azivor

Curiosity is better with a test.

The interesting part of AI progress is what it lets you attempt. Azivor helps students connect a new possibility to something they can actually make, learn, or improve.

Purpose

Why this exists

Azivor is a student-led project built around a simple path: discover what is possible, understand what it means for you, and put it to work. We share concrete examples, practical workflows, and the decisions behind the result.

A finished artifact is only part of the aim. The student should also understand the important choices, check the result, and be able to try a related task independently.

See a build

Human agency

Reach further. Keep your judgment.

Our developing learning framework is the Human Loop: think, delegate, inspect, explain, verify, and own. It asks students to choose what AI should do while preserving the reasoning and practice they need to build.

For students and parents, the question is what kind of thinking a workflow gives the student a chance to practise. Hints can support a first attempt; critique can sharpen a draft; execution can help when the student knows how to evaluate it.

Explore the Human Loop

Standards

Show the work. State the limits.

We distinguish a working example from a broader claim. Builds describe what AI contributed, what required human judgment, and what still needs work. New capabilities earn attention through useful outcomes, rather than release headlines alone.

Azivor is early in development. The learning framework is a direction we are putting into practice, not a validated course or a promise of improved learning outcomes.
